### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__ActionButtonProps__patch.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in rowDeclarativeUpdate))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in rowDeclarativeUpdate))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in rowDeclarativeUpdate))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in rowDeclarativeUpdate))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__ActionButtonProps__patch.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `480a0ab6071420406afa6b252d3c6908ab8b3d5c` — the merge of head `daf710a3aa825ecfc9a34c3c6a7e7c7f79fec7b6` into base `9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 480a0ab6071420406afa6b252d3c6908ab8b3d5c && git checkout 480a0ab6071420406afa6b252d3c6908ab8b3d5c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6 daf710a3aa825ecfc9a34c3c6a7e7c7f79fec7b6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6 && git merge --no-ff daf710a3aa825ecfc9a34c3c6a7e7c7f79fec7b6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9112bcd887dbe3716466a55637df43fde00655a6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The head is a merge commit (parents `d6976f1c92` and `538f923cb9`); the one conflict resolution the newest report names (`registry.ts.template`, STEP18_RATIONALE) was read in the head tree. Check-runs: every required context is `success` (Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core with its six shards, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard), as are Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Build Docs and every Lint and Type Check lane; the only `skipped` runs are the full-battery-only jobs (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood shards, Temporal Conformance, packed-tarball smoke) and the re-triggered label/size duplicates. Not a governed-surface diff (no path under docs/adr, .claude, .github/workflows, skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, NORTH-STAR); head repo is the base repo; 1,285 changed lines, under the 3,000 ceiling.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or surface change the diff implies, judged against the cited code.

1. **A page action row's own `patch` is refused (narrowing) — RIGHT.** `component.zod.ts` replaces the by-reference `actionPatch` with `rowPatchRetired(owner)`, a `retiredKey()` tombstone on `action:button` (:4021), `action:icon` (:4121) and the shared `action:group` / `action:menu` member (:4271). `retiredKey()` (`shared/retired-key.ts`) is `z.never({ error }).optional()`, so a present value yields ONE `invalid_type` issue carrying the prescription and the input type is the `never`-marked object, which is what the new pin asserts (`fails tsc at the authoring site`) and what the lint pins assert at `properties.patch` and `properties.actions.0.patch` with severity `error`. The premise is true in the cited code: at the pin, `ActionRunner.executeUpdateOperation` (:1782-:1810) reads `action.patch` only into `written` for the Undo snapshot and posts `wire = { ...collected }`; `createServerActionHandler` (:208-:243) posts `{ recordId, params }` to `/api/v1/actions/OBJECT/NAME`; on this side `declarativeUpdateWrite` (`runtime/src/action-execution.ts:2213`) builds `{ ...declaration.patch, ...params }` from the declaration `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` resolved by name (ADR-0110 D2, read at its section heading: "Resolve, then address: declaration first"). The row's `patch` reaches no request. The prescription closes with the standardized `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence, and no leftover `actionPatch` or `staticParams` reference survives in `packages/spec/src` or `packages/lint/src`.

2. **`operation: 'update'` on a row with no (or an empty) `name` is refused at `name` (narrowing) — RIGHT, as reading A.** `action-declarative-update.ts` rule 4 on a `writesNamedAction` surface asks `namesAction(data.name)`; previously a nameless row with a `patch` or non-empty params parsed. The refused shape never worked: the dispatch at the pin returns `Action has no name — a server action must declare one` before any request (serverActionHandler :211-:213), and the route has no declaration to resolve. The seat's answer that reading A stands is recorded in report `6259634070`; the built judge matches it, and the PR body's own paragraph explains the choice.

3. **A named row with `operation: 'update'`, no `patch` and no `params` now parses (widening) — RIGHT, and declared.** Before, rule 4 refused it at `patch` as having nothing to write; its write is the named declaration's `patch`, which `declarativeUpdateWrite` performs with an empty params bag. The PR body and the changeset both name this direction, so `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is measured, not assumed.

4. **A node's static object `params` no longer count as the row's write but remain accepted — RIGHT.** `paramsWrite` drops the `staticParams` arm; the three `params` describes now say the values ride the request and are written only where the named action declares them. That is the route as it is: `actions.ts:673-:679` runs `enforceActionParams` (ADR-0104 D2) before the handler and answers a 400 on an undeclared key, on a param-less update too. The describe's admission that the name-to-declaration cross-reference is one "this row cannot see" is accurate; see ③ F1.

5. **`ActionSchema` is behaviour-neutral — RIGHT.** The one `action.zod.ts` line renames the descriptor's `staticParams: false` to `writesNamedAction: false`. On that surface rule 1 still runs (`!surface.writesNamedAction && data.patch !== undefined`) and rule 4's `paramsWrite(params)` reduces to the same test the old `staticParams: false` arm computed (an array `params` with a positive length, nothing else). The pin `ActionSchema.patch is untouched` holds it. `DeclarativeUpdateSurface` is not exported from `spec/ui`'s index and appears in no `api-surface` shard, so the field rename is an internal change, not a public-surface one.

6. **The D2 conversion `page-action-row-patch-removed` — RIGHT.** `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` (the same stamp as 33 sibling 18-train entries; the type's docblock in `conversions/types.ts` says it is the artifact-ingestion floor and is pinned by the census test, which Test Core ran green). Scoped by component `type` through `ACTION_RUNNER_BLOCK_TYPES` and `ACTION_CONTAINER_BLOCK_TYPES`, never by key name, so an open-namespace `acme:quick_edit` keeps its own `patch`. `mapPageComponents` (`conversions/walk.ts:31`) visits regions, named `slots` and nested trees, which is the reach the fixture exercises (button, bare icon, group member, nested menu member, slotted icon); `stripKeys` emits one notice per deleted key and returns the same reference when nothing is touched, so `expectedNotices: 5`, the by-reference control and idempotence follow. Order 70 is the list's new maximum; duplicate orders already exist in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`, so uniqueness was never a constraint.

7. **The ledger rows — RIGHT.** `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `ui/ActionButtonProps:patch` and `ui/ActionIconProps:patch`, the same spelling as the sibling `18.ui__Action__aria.ts`; `authorable-surface/ui.json` marks exactly those two rows `[RETIRED]`, and the member rows have no surface entry, so the two-key registration is correct rather than short. The `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` JOIN row names the family under `page-action-row-patch-removed` with the two tombstones and the two member refusals. The `liveness/page.json` edit touches the `regions` row's note only, status and `verifiedAt` unmoved; Spec property liveness is green.

8. **The D3 entry and the STEP18 fragment — RIGHT.** `ui-page-action-row-patch-retired` carries every required `SemanticMigration` field (id, surface without backticks, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria); it names the judgement the strip cannot make (moving stripped values onto the named action). The fragment with the same id sits at order 104 beside #24417's order-103 fragment; the template differs from base `538f923cb9` by these 15 added lines only. The three sibling 18 D3 texts (`operation-declared`, `declarative-update-rules`, `action-group-menu-members-typed`) are re-trued so the 18 upgrade guide no longer prescribes a row `patch` or lists `patch?` among member keys; left as they were, they would have contradicted the tombstone.

9. **The pinned sibling at `0707b4ae37` keeps building — RIGHT (P3 verified independently).** objectui's non-test source reaches the row types only as `SpecActionButtonProps['size']` (`packages/types/src/ui-action.ts:900`) and as whole schemas through `stripImportedDefaults` / `propsBag` / `flatPropRefusals` in `public-blocks.zod.ts`, helpers that already compose tombstoned rows (`page:header`, `element:number`); `ui-action.ts:647`'s `patch?: SpecAction['patch']` is `ActionSchema`'s, untouched; every `ComponentPropsMap['action:...']` mention in non-test source is a comment. `packages/types` builds with `tsc`, so this is the compile path that matters, and it is clean. The Console Pin Gate job (`ci.yml`, `console-pin`) runs `scripts/build-console.sh` plus `check:console-sha` and `check:console-injection`, a build and no objectui test run, so the retirement creates no main-red at the pin.

10. **Describes and generated docs — RIGHT.** The three `operation`, three `name` and two node `params` describes say what the route does; `check:docs` (in the TypeScript Type Check job) and `check:authorable-surface` are green, so `component.mdx` and `ui.json` are the generators' output.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24394-page-action-row-patch-retired.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, body opening with **BREAKING**, the FROM → TO table (three rows), the one-line fix, the exact prescription an author sees, the retirement kit, and the `adr-0087: registered page-action-row-patch-removed, ui-page-action-row-patch-retired` marker that `check:adr-0087-registration` read green. This matches what the diff publishes: the only released package with a source change is `@objectstack/spec` (`packages/lint` changes are test files; `content/docs` is not published). `minor` for a BREAKING accept-set narrowing is the 18-train convention stated on the sibling retired-keys entry (accept-set narrowings ride minor releases) and satisfies the rule that a `yes` takes at least `minor`. The changeset names no model identifier.

`Clause-②:` line — `yes (narrowing)`, present and identical on the PR body and the changeset; both directions are measured on the built rows (narrowing in ① 1-2, widening in ① 3), so the arm is correct and the claim's provisional line stands unamended.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report `6259032573` deviations, report `6259634070` deviations), each answered:

- File-surface breaches named by the dev: `action.zod.ts` (one behaviour-neutral line, ① 5), three sibling D3 entries (① 8), two lint test files, `vitest.repo-tests.json` (the repo-project listing that `check:cross-package-test-inputs` holds), the removal-version pin, the unknown-members ledger. Each is required by the kit; none touches a hold-off (`ActionSchema`'s rules and texts, `packages/runtime`, objectui, ADR-0104, `stack.zod.ts`, release notes all untouched). Accepted.
- H4 refuted in form (no per-key liveness row exists; the page ledger walks top-level props): the `regions` note was re-trued instead. Accepted.
- `test:repo` narrowed locally to the new pin and its sibling under the 10-minute cap; Test Core on the head ran the full set green. Accepted.
- `main` not merged before opening, then merged at the seat's patch round through `os-regen-merge.sh` with one conflict (STEP18_RATIONALE): both fragments kept, #24417's byte-for-byte, this card's renumbered 103 to 104. The renumber was not required (that list already carries three fragments at order 95) but is harmless. `origin/main` moved twice since (`4d12b23f04`, `fa26308bb0`), 0 overlap with this diff. Accepted.
- Harness attribution overridden by AGENTS.md's model-free trailer pair and session-URL footer; container restart mid-run with verification re-run from a committed state; one gate batch over the cap, the killed gate re-run whole. Accepted.
- `pr_body_amend_for_the_seat`: applied. The body now reads order 104 and says the checklist gate is not per-PR CI (its watchdog carries #24438), which the head's green Lint and Repo Gates confirms.

`open_questions`, both answered by the seat and recorded in report `6259634070`:

- Q1, the row half of rule 4: reading A stands (nameless update row refused at `name`). The built judge matches it (① 2). Closed.
- Q2, a validate-time cross-reference from a row's `name` to a declared `operation: 'update'` action and from its static `params` to that action's declared params: the seat ruled "noted, not filed". Recorded as answered. **F1, escalated as a recommendation, not a FAIL:** after this PR the row's entire write is a reference the spec cannot resolve, and an AI-authored row with a `name` that resolves nowhere, or static params the action does not declare, fails only at click (a 404 or the ADR-0104 D2 400 with no write). The dev's option A names an existing walk (`packages/lint/src/validate-action-name-refs.ts`) that already resolves names for four other blocks, so the fix is located and cheap. Under Prime Directive 10 this reads as a metadata-authoring trap with a located fix; a p3 card is the right carrier. The PR itself is right without it, and the gap predates it (no action row's `name` was cross-referenced before).

Reviewer's own flags:

- F2 (objectui follow-up, the seat's at landing, out of this PR's surface): at the pin the four renderers forward `patch`, the runner and `predicate-fields.ts:155` read it for Undo, and the registry publishes a `patch` input on `action:button` / `action:icon`, so the tracked `sdui.manifest.json` still advertises it to the html-tier JSX gate until the pin moves. Once objectui adopts a spec with this tombstone, its `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` pin `the harvested tombstoned keys are recognised, not exempted — and not published either` reds on that input; and after the retirement the Undo snapshot of a row covers only the collected params, not the named action's `patch` the route wrote. Neither affects the Console Pin Gate (build only, ① 9). The card the seat files should carry all three.
- F3 (note): the D3 entry omits `conversionIds`. The strip-class siblings (`page-header-show-star-retired`, `ui-record-json-retired`, `ui-marketplace-installed-list-retired`) omit it too, and the new pin reads the D2 id from the entry's prose; convention held, nothing to change.
- F4 (note): `namesAction` admits a whitespace-only `name`, exactly as the console's `if (!actionName)` does; the same class as F1 and not a defect of this diff.
